events.title: The Magonids
events.text: The family of Mago leads Carthage's armies and politics for three generations.

events.title: Gadir
events.text: The old Phoenician city of Gadir, with its temple of Melqart, guards the Atlantic gateway.

events.title: Lixus
events.text: One of the oldest Phoenician towns of the Atlantic stands above the Loukkos estuary.

events.title: Mogador
events.text: An island trading post off Essaouira, the southernmost Phoenician site yet found.

events.title: War in Sardinia
events.text: Mago's son Hasdrubal leads Carthage's long campaigns in Sardinia, where he dies of his wounds.

events.title: Tartessos fades
events.text: The rich Tartessian culture of the lower Guadalquivir declines, and Gadir takes over its trade.

events.title: Dorieus expelled
events.text: Carthage and the Libyan Macae drive out a Spartan colony planted on the Cinyps river.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: By Carthage's first treaty with Rome, Roman ships may not sail beyond the Fair Promontory.

events.title: Hanno sets sail
events.text: The Periplus tells of sixty ships of fifty oars carrying thirty thousand men and women.

events.title: Through the Pillars
events.text: Hanno's fleet passes the Strait of Gibraltar into the outer sea.

events.title: Thymiaterion
events.text: Two days beyond the Pillars, Hanno founds his first town above a wide plain.

events.title: Cape Soloeis
events.text: On a wooded headland, probably Cape Cantin, the colonists raise a temple to Poseidon.

events.title: Five new towns
events.text: Past a lagoon full of elephants, Hanno settles colonists in five towns along the coast.

events.title: The Lixus river
events.text: At a great river, perhaps the Draa, Hanno befriends nomads and takes interpreters on board.

events.title: Cerne
events.text: Colonists are left on a small island in a bay: Herne Island by Dakhla, or Mogador.

events.title: River of crocodiles
events.text: A wide river teeming with crocodiles and hippopotamuses, most probably the Senegal.

events.title: The Western Horn
events.text: In a great gulf, the coast fills at night with fires, flutes, cymbals and drums.

events.title: Chariot of the Gods?
events.text: Mount Kakulima in Guinea, one candidate for the burning peak Hanno saw from the sea.

events.title: The Southern Horn
events.text: On many readings, Hanno's last landfall lies in Sherbro Sound, Sierra Leone.

events.title: Mount Cameroon
events.text: The active volcano, over four thousand metres high, is the 'Chariot of the Gods' on the longest reading.

events.title: The Gorillai
events.text: On an island in the last gulf, here on the longest reading, Hanno's men capture three hairy women and kill them.

events.title: The voyage recorded
events.text: Back in Carthage, the account is set up in the temple of Baal Hammon, the skins in Tanit's.

events.title: Himilco sails north
events.text: Pliny says Himilco was sent from Gadir at the same time to explore the coasts of Europe.

events.title: The Sacred Cape
events.text: Himilco's ships round the great headland of Cape St Vincent and turn north.

events.title: A sluggish sea
events.text: Avienus quotes Himilco on windless calms, weed that holds back ships, shallows and sea monsters.

events.title: The Oestrymnides
events.text: Islands rich in tin and lead, four months' sailing from Gadir, perhaps off Brittany.

events.title: Albion
events.text: Near the tin islands lie the island of the Albiones and the 'Holy Island' of the Hierni.

events.title: Battle of Himera
events.text: Gelon of Syracuse crushes a great Carthaginian army in Sicily; its general Hamilcar dies.

events.title: The indemnity
events.text: Carthage pays Syracuse two thousand talents of silver and turns from Sicily for seventy years.

events.title: Sataspes
events.text: A Persian noble sails past Cape Soloeis and south for months, then turns back; Xerxes has him executed.

events.title: Kerkouane
events.text: A Punic town on Cap Bon flourishes, with private baths in its houses and purple-dye workshops.

events.title: Hamilcar's sons
events.text: Justin names Himilco, Hanno and Gisgo among the Magonid generals; some see the navigators here.

events.title: The hinterland
events.text: Carthage stops paying rent to the Libyans and builds an African domain of farms.

events.title: Gadir's salt fish
events.text: Fish-salting works around Gadir send amphorae of tuna and sauce across the Mediterranean.

events.title: Leptis
events.text: The Punic emporium of Leptis trades with the Garamantes of the Sahara.

events.title: Ebusus
events.text: Carthage's colony on Ibiza grows into a busy port, with one of the great Punic cemeteries.

events.title: Silent trade
events.text: Herodotus tells of Carthaginians leaving goods on a beach beyond the Pillars and finding gold beside them.

events.title: Herodotus writes
events.text: Herodotus finishes his Histories; he knows of Carthage's Atlantic trade but not of Hanno.

chartNote: Share of the area of 22 present-day countries, from Britain to Cameroon; regions are today's boundaries. A deliberate simplification: Punic presence was a string of coastal posts, yet whole countries are coloured. The voyages are dated c. 500 BC by convention, and how far Hanno sailed is disputed: the map shows the cautious and the maximal readings side by side, and Himilco's reach is unknown.
